newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE insurer calls for large scale mergers.
newsitem.headline: UAE insurer calls for large scale mergers.

text.p: Local insurers in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) should consider mergers to fight fierce competition brought about by the country's accession to the World Trade Organisation (WTO), an insurance executive said in remarks published on Wednesday.

"Insurers in the United Arab Emirates should gear up to face the challenges of an open services sector under the World Trade Organisation," Fareed Lutfi, executive director of Alliance Insurance Co, said in an interview with al-Bayan daily.

"Excess liquidity in the UAE makes raising additional capital easy, but the answer is in mergers to stand up in the face of foreign competition," the head of the 25 million dirham ($6.8 million) firm added.
The UAE, which is trying to diversify its economy away from oil, became a WTO member in December 1995.
Nineteen national companies and 27 foreign firms operate in the UAE insurance market.
Analysts said Western insurers could carve a bigger niche of the market for themselves under the WTO accords by offering investment schemes as add-ons to traditional policies.
They said foreign insurers could offer cheaper deals for local clients because their overheads and other burdens were borne by a network of international profit centres.

Some 70 percent of the 2.2 billion dirhams insurance premiums in the UAE in 1995 went to local insurers, but analysts said profit margins were slim because local insurers concentrated mostly on the low-profit end of the market specialising in car, property and general insurance.
Lutfi said half of the national insurance companies were capitalised at less then 50 million dirhams each.
